session_1.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
session_1.text: [user, notes] LANTERN (CVN-221-02) status, 02-Mar-2026. Phase II, open-label, two-cohort study of CVN-221 (oral selective FGFR2 inhibitor) in previously treated intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. Cohort A = FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements, Cohort B = other FGFR2 alterations (activating mutations, amplifications). Primary endpoint ORR by BICR per RECIST 1.1. 14 subjects dosed so far, all under protocol v2.0 at 160 mg QD continuous, 28-day cycles. Five sites active (101 Calder Cancer Center, 102 St. Aldric Medical Center, 103 Lakeshore University Hospital, 104 Pinecrest Oncology Institute, 105 Bayridge Regional Cancer Center); site 106 Mercer Valley Health still in contracting. Enrollment target is 84 (Cohort A 48, Cohort B 36). Database lock target 30-Nov-2026. Hyperphosphatemia signal: 3 of 14 subjects with Grade 3 events (101-002, 102-003, 104-005). Ilse Varga (medical monitor) wants Amendment 1 to lower the starting dose.

session_1.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
session_1.text: Before we start on anything else: whenever you summarize enrollment for me, give it to me as a table sorted by site number, with separate Cohort A and Cohort B columns and a total row. No prose paragraphs around it. I paste those straight into the steering committee deck and I hate reformatting.

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text: [assistant, chat] Understood. session_1.speaker: Maya Lindqvist
session_1.text: OK. Now help me with the rationale paragraph for Amendment 1. Proposal from Ilse: drop the starting dose from 160 mg to 120 mg QD, still continuous. Dose level -1 becomes 80 mg and level -2 becomes 60 mg (under v2.0 they were 120 mg and 80 mg). Also start sevelamer when serum phosphate exceeds 5.5 mg/dL instead of the current 7.0 mg/dL trigger.

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text: [assistant, chat] Draft rationale (Section 1.3, Amendment 1): 'Among the first 14 subjects treated at 160 mg QD, 3 (21.4%) experienced CTCAE v5.0 Grade 3 hyperphosphatemia, and 5 (35.7%) required dose interruption within Cycle 1. Preliminary PK indicates steady-state AUC at 160 mg exceeds the exposure associated with maximal FGFR2 target inhibition in the Phase I population by approximately 1.6-fold. Consistent with the on-target mechanism of FGFR inhibition, the starting dose is reduced to 120 mg QD continuous (28-day cycles), with dose level -1 at 80 mg and -2 at 60 mg. Phosphate-lowering therapy (sevelamer) will be initiated at serum phosphate >5.5 mg/dL (previously >7.0 mg/dL).' Suggest you have Rohan confirm the 1.6-fold figure before it goes to Meridian; I took it from the PK slide you shared, not from a final report.

session_4.text: Can you calculate Cycle 2 dose intensity for 101-011? Planned 120 mg QD for 28 days. She held doses on days 9 to 11 for Grade 2 stomatitis and resumed at 120 mg on day 12. No other missed doses per the diary.

session_4.speaker: assistant
session_4.text: [assistant, chat] Planned Cycle 2 dose: 120 mg x 28 days = 3,360 mg. Doses missed on days 9, 10 and 11 = 3 days, so 25 days x 120 mg = 3,000 mg received. Relative dose intensity = 3,000 / 3,360 = 89.3%. This is above the 80% threshold the SAP uses for the 'adequate exposure' sensitivity analysis, so 101-011 stays in that population for Cycle 2. If her diary later shows a vomited dose, it still counts as taken per SAP section 9.2.

domain: molecular biology & genomics (CRISPR screens and RNA-seq)

session_1.speaker: Lena Varga
session_1.text: New project, keeping records with you from the start. I'm a staff scientist in Wei Chen's lab. Plan: a genome-wide CRISPR knockout resistance screen in HAP1 cells against the compound AZ-5417, a quinone-containing investigational agent, followed by RNA-seq of the validated knockouts. Library is Brunello, 77,441 sgRNAs over 19,114 genes, lot L-88213. Target library coverage 500x at every step. Planned MOI 0.3, puromycin selection at 1.0 ug/mL starting 48 h post-transduction. Screen identifier SCR-01, transduction planned for 2026-01-14.

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text: [assistant, chat] Logged: SCR-01, HAP1, Brunello lot L-88213, 500x coverage target, MOI 0.3, puromycin 1.0 ug/mL from 48 h, transduction 2026-01-14, compound AZ-5417. Two flags before you start. (1) 1.0 ug/mL puromycin is a plausible HAP1 number but it is passage- and serum-dependent; if you have not run a kill curve on this exact passage you are guessing. (2) At 500x coverage with 77,441 guides you need roughly 39 million selected cells per replicate, which drives your flask count more than anything else in the protocol - check that against your incubator space before the transduction, not after.

session_1.speaker: Lena Varga
session_1.text: Standing request on format. When you give me a protocol or a protocol change, give it as numbered steps, and put every concentration in bold and in ug/mL - not molar, not nM, not 'per flask'. I transcribe these onto the bench sheet and molar units are how we poisoned a whole plate last year.

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text: [assistant, chat] Understood: numbered steps, concentrations bold and in ug/mL. Example in that format for the selection step as you have it now. 1. Seed HAP1 at 2.5e6 cells per T-175, 10 flasks per replicate. 2. Transduce with Brunello lot L-88213 at MOI 0.3 in the presence of polybrene **8 ug/mL**. 3. At 24 h, full medium change. 4. At 48 h, begin selection with puromycin **1.0 ug/mL**. 5. Maintain selection 7 days, feeding every 48 h, keeping **1.0 ug/mL** at each feed. 6. At day 7 harvest a 500x reference aliquot before splitting into compound and vehicle arms.

session_1.speaker: lab meeting notes
session_1.text: [attachment, meeting] Chen lab meeting, 2026-01-12. Varga presents the AZ-5417 screen plan. Chen asks for two biological replicates minimum, three preferred. Analysis to be done with Raul Mendes (computational core); Mendes will set up MAGeCK. Dana Pryce (Genomics Core) holds our sequencing slots - note Dana Pryce is the core manager, not Dan Pryor in facilities, who handles the freezers. Collaborator Dr Ilse Brandt (Utrecht) will supply the AZ-5417 and the matched inactive analogue AZ-5418.

session_1.speaker: Ilse Brandt
session_1.text: [attachment, email] From: Ilse Brandt (Utrecht). Subject: AZ-5417 shipment. Lena - shipped today, arrives 2026-01-13. 25 mg AZ-5417 free base, lot AZB-2211, and 25 mg of the inactive analogue AZ-5418, lot AZB-2214. Store desiccated at -20 C, make 10 mM stock in DMSO. The IC50 in HAP1 from our hands is 0.8 uM at 72 h, but we never ran it past 96 h. Good luck - please keep the lot numbers on everything, we are tracking a synthesis batch difference.

session_1.speaker: Lena Varga
session_1.text: [user, notes] Reagent register, screen SCR-01. Brunello library lot L-88213, titre 4.1e7 TU/mL per the core's p24 estimate. AZ-5417 lot AZB-2211. AZ-5418 (inactive analogue) lot AZB-2214. Polybrene 8 ug/mL working. Puromycin stock 10 mg/mL, working 1.0 ug/mL for HAP1. Note for contrast: our HEK293T packaging line is selected at 1.0 ug/mL too but blasticidin is 10 ug/mL - do not mix those two numbers up on the bench sheet.

session_1.speaker: Lena Varga
session_1.text: Transduction is Wednesday 2026-01-14 and the first sequencing slot Dana has is the week of 2026-02-02. Is that enough of a gap for a 7-day selection plus 10 days of compound pressure?

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text: [assistant, chat] It is tight but it fits: transduction 2026-01-14, selection to 2026-01-21, split into arms, 10 days of AZ-5417 pressure to 2026-01-31, harvest and gDNA extraction 2026-02-01, library PCR 2026-02-02 for a slot that week. The risk is that you have no slack for a repeat PCR. Build one day of slack by harvesting the reference aliquot on day 7 as planned rather than pooling it at the end - if the final PCR fails you still have the reference and only need to redo one arm.

session_2.speaker: Lena Varga
session_2.text: SCR-01 is a failure and I want it on the record as such. Two problems. The functional titre was far below the p24 estimate: measured MOI came out at 0.12, not the 0.3 I planned, so my selected population is about 2.4 million cells per replicate instead of 39 million. That is 31x coverage, not 500x. Second, the puromycin at 1.0 ug/mL did not fully kill the untransduced control plate even at day 7 - about 15% survival. Calling SCR-01 dead rather than sequencing something I cannot interpret.

session_2.speaker: assistant
session_2.text: [assistant, chat] Agreed, do not sequence it - at 31x coverage the dropout distribution is noise and a negative result would be uninterpretable. Both failures have the same root cause worth noting: you took two numbers from elsewhere rather than measuring them on this passage. Recommendation for the repeat, in your format. 1. Titre the library by functional transduction on HAP1, not by p24, using a 6-point dilution and reading puromycin-resistant colonies at day 7. 2. Run a kill curve before anything else: 8 points of puromycin from **0 ug/mL** to **4.0 ug/mL** in 0.5 ug/mL steps, on the same passage you will screen, scored at 72 h and at day 7. Pick the lowest concentration giving 100% death of untransduced cells by day 7, not by 72 h. 3. Only then set the MOI.

session_2.speaker: Lena Varga
session_2.text: [user, notes] SCR-01 post mortem. Failure mode: insufficient library representation (measured MOI 0.12, achieved coverage 31x against a 500x target) compounded by incomplete puromycin selection at 1.0 ug/mL (15% survival of untransduced controls at day 7). Cells discarded 2026-01-19. gDNA not extracted. No sequencing run consumed. Dana Pryce informed that the 2026-02-02 slot will not be used; she is holding it for the repeat.

session_2.speaker: Dana Pryce
session_2.text: [attachment, email] From: Dana Pryce (Genomics Core). Subject: re: slot. No problem holding the week of 2026-02-02 for you. For planning: our NextSeq 2000 has a P3 kit available that week; the NovaSeq X runs are batched and the next one after that is the week of 2026-03-16. Core time is billed at the usual rate and I log it against your project code; the kill-curve plate reading does not count as core time, that is your own bench work.

session_2.speaker: Lena Varga
session_2.text: Kill curve goes up Thursday. Eight points, 0 to 4.0 ug/mL in 0.5 steps, as you said, same passage, scored at 72 h and day 7. Untransduced HAP1 only, three wells per point.

session_2.speaker: assistant
session_2.text: [assistant, chat] One addition: include a transduced-and-selected well at each concentration too, not just untransduced. You need to know the concentration that kills all untransduced cells AND that your transduced cells tolerate for 7 days without visible stress - those are two different thresholds and the gap between them is your working window. Three wells per point is the minimum; if you have plate space use four, because at the low end you will be counting survivors by eye.

session_2.speaker: SOP-HAP1-CRISPR-v1.md
session_2.text: [attachment, document] Excerpt, SOP-HAP1-CRISPR-v1.md, Section 4 Selection. 4.1 At 48 h post-transduction, replace medium with complete IMDM containing puromycin at 1.0 ug/mL. 4.2 Feed every 48 h maintaining 1.0 ug/mL. 4.3 Selection duration 7 days. 4.4 Untransduced control plate must show 100% death by day 7; if survival exceeds 1%, selection is invalid. Section 6 Harvest. 6.1 Pellet 4e7 cells per arm. 6.2 Lyse in proteinase K buffer at 56 C for 1 h with intermittent vortexing.

session_2.speaker: Lena Varga
session_2.text: Yes - and SOP v1 clearly needs updating, since 4.1 is the 1.0 ug/mL number that just failed its own criterion in 4.4. I will revise the SOP once the kill curve is read rather than guessing twice.

session_2.speaker: Lena Varga
session_2.text: [user, voice] Dictating in the tissue culture room. First screen is dead, measured M O I was zero point one two, coverage thirty one x. Kill curve Thursday, eight points, zero to four. Tell Wei at lab meeting rather than by email, he takes failed screens better in person. Ask Ilse whether the compound is stable for more than two weeks in D M S O at minus twenty.

session_3.speaker: Lena Varga
session_3.text: Kill curve read. At 72 h everything above 1.0 ug/mL looks dead, but at day 7 there are survivors up to and including 1.0 ug/mL. The lowest concentration with zero untransduced survivors at day 7 is 1.5 ug/mL, and transduced cells tolerate 1.5 ug/mL for 7 days with no visible stress. So I am changing the protocol: puromycin selection goes from 1.0 ug/mL to 1.5 ug/mL.

session_3.speaker: assistant
session_3.text: [assistant, chat] Updated: puromycin selection **1.5 ug/mL** (was **1.0 ug/mL**). That is exactly why the day-7 read matters - at 72 h your old number looked fine. One caution: 1.5 ug/mL is the lowest concentration with zero survivors in three wells, which means your confidence interval on 'zero' is not tight. If the repeat screen again shows any survival on the untransduced plate, go up rather than extending the selection, because extending selection costs you library representation.

session_3.speaker: Lena Varga
session_3.text: [user, notes] SOP-HAP1-CRISPR-v2. Section 4.1 now reads: puromycin 1.5 ug/mL from 48 h post-transduction. 4.2 maintain 1.5 ug/mL at each feed. Historical note kept deliberately: v1 specified 1.0 ug/mL, which failed criterion 4.4 in SCR-01. Functional titration of Brunello lot L-88213 on HAP1 gave 8.9e6 TU/mL, not the 4.1e7 TU/mL p24 estimate - a 4.6-fold overestimate, which explains the MOI miss.

session_3.speaker: Lena Varga
session_3.text: Second standing request, about results. When you give me screen or RNA-seq results, give me a plain table with gene symbol, log2 fold change and FDR, and nothing else - no ranks, no pathway columns, no descriptions. And no plots in the chat; I make my own volcano plots in R and yours just cost me scrolling.

session_3.speaker: assistant
session_3.text: [assistant, chat] Noted: results as a three-column table, gene symbol, log2FC, FDR, nothing else, and no plots. I will also not describe what the genes do unless you ask.

session_3.speaker: Raul Mendes
session_3.text: [attachment, email] From: Raul Mendes. Subject: analysis setup. Lena - I have MAGeCK 0.5.9.4 installed in the project conda environment, with the Brunello library file mapped to GRCh38. For the screen I will run both the RRA test and the MLE test so we can compare. For the later RNA-seq I have nf-core/rnaseq 3.12.0 pinned with the Ensembl 110 annotation. Send me the sample sheet as soon as you know the arm structure.

session_3.speaker: Lena Varga
session_3.text: SCR-02 planning. Transduction 2026-01-28, this time MOI 0.3 using the functional titre of 8.9e6 TU/mL, puromycin 1.5 ug/mL, three biological replicates, 500x coverage target, 10 days of AZ-5417 at 0.8 uM against a vehicle arm, harvest 2026-02-08.

session_3.speaker: assistant
session_3.text: [assistant, chat] That plan is internally consistent. The one number I would reconsider is the compound concentration: Brandt's IC50 of 0.8 uM at 72 h came from her hands and her passage, and for a 10-day resistance screen you want roughly the IC80 to IC90 at your own 7-day timepoint, which is usually appreciably above the 72 h IC50. Run a 5-point dose response alongside the selection week so that the number you use on day 7 is yours, not hers.

session_3.speaker: Lena Varga
session_3.text: Good point, running the dose response in parallel during selection week. If it lands much above 0.8 uM I will use my own number and record both.

session_4.speaker: Lena Varga
session_4.text: SCR-02 is through selection and looks right: untransduced control plate 100% dead at day 7 at 1.5 ug/mL, measured MOI 0.29, estimated 41 million selected cells per replicate, so about 530x coverage. My own dose response gave a 7-day IC80 of 1.6 uM, double Brandt's 72 h IC50, so I am running the compound arm at 1.6 uM and recording both numbers.

session_4.speaker: assistant
session_4.text: [assistant, chat] Good - 530x against a 500x target, and the compound concentration is now yours. Record the 1.6 uM in the reagent register next to Brandt's 0.8 uM so that six months from now nobody reads 0.8 as the screen concentration.

session_4.speaker: Lena Varga
session_4.text: Mendes is asking which MAGeCK test to use as primary. He has 0.5.9.4 with both RRA and MLE available. Three replicates, paired vehicle and compound arms from the same transduction, plus a day-7 reference. What do you recommend as the primary analysis and what thresholds?

session_4.speaker: assistant
session_4.text: [assistant, chat] Recommendation: use MAGeCK MLE as the primary analysis with a paired design matrix, treating replicate as a covariate, and keep RRA only as a sanity check in the supplement. Thresholds: call a gene a hit at FDR < 0.1 with at least 3 of the 4 sgRNAs moving in the same direction. Reasons: your arms are paired by transduction, which MLE can use and RRA cannot; RRA's permutation null is poorly behaved when a handful of guides have very high counts, which happens in resistance screens because the resistant clones dominate; and the 3-of-4 guide requirement is what protects you from a single off-target guide carrying a gene. Do not lower FDR to 0.05 here - with three replicates you will lose real hits.

session_4.speaker: Lena Varga
session_4.text: [user, notes] Analysis decision recorded: MAGeCK MLE primary, paired design, replicate as covariate, FDR < 0.1, at least 3 of 4 sgRNAs concordant. RRA in the supplement only. Mendes agrees. Distractor to avoid in the writeup: the lab's older papers used RRA with FDR < 0.05, that is not what we are doing here.

session_4.speaker: Dana Pryce
session_4.text: [attachment, email] From: Dana Pryce (Genomics Core). Subject: RUN-2601 scheduled. Your libraries are queued as RUN-2601 on the NextSeq 2000, P3 300-cycle kit, loading 2026-02-05, data out 2026-02-07. 12 libraries: 3 replicates x (vehicle, compound) plus 3 day-7 references, single-end 75 with the standard sgRNA read structure. I have logged 4.0 hours of core time against your project code for the QC, pooling and loading.

session_4.speaker: seq-pipeline
session_4.text: [tool, agent_log] RUN-2601 | instrument NextSeq 2000 | kit P3 300cyc | loaded 2026-02-05T16:22 | 12 libraries | status COMPLETE | 1.21e9 reads passing filter | Q30 94.1% | per-library range 78M-124M reads | index balance OK | note: library 11 (reference rep 3) at 78M, below the 90M target but usable

session_4.speaker: Lena Varga
session_4.text: RUN-2601 done, 12 libraries, data with Mendes. First real data on this project. Core time on this run was 4.0 hours.

session_4.speaker: assistant
session_4.text: [assistant, chat] Logged: RUN-2601, NextSeq 2000, 12 libraries, 4.0 hours of core time. Before you look at hits, check two QC numbers with Mendes: the Gini index of the day-7 reference libraries, which should be below about 0.1 for a healthy Brunello representation, and the fraction of guides with zero counts in the reference, which should be under 1%. If either is off, the hit list is not trustworthy no matter how good it looks.

session_4.speaker: Lena Varga
session_4.text: [user, voice] Dictating. Screen zero two is sequenced, twelve libraries, run twenty six oh one. Puromycin one point five works. My own I C eighty is one point six micromolar, use mine not Ilse's. Ask Mendes for the Gini index and the zero count fraction before I let myself look at the gene list.

session_5.speaker: Lena Varga
session_5.text: Unrelated to the analysis but it matters for the record: we had a freezer alarm on 2026-02-09, the -80 in the corridor, which is where the gDNA from SCR-02 and the backup cell pellets live. Dan Pryor in facilities says the compressor ran hot for an unknown period overnight. Freezer logged -62 C at the alarm.

session_5.speaker: assistant
session_5.text: [assistant, chat] At -62 C for a few hours gDNA is fine - double-stranded DNA in TE tolerates that without detectable degradation - but the cell pellets are a different matter if they were viable-frozen in DMSO, since partial thaw and refreeze will cost you viability rather than nucleic acid. Practical plan: run a TapeStation or gel on one gDNA aliquot per arm three days after the alarm, so 2026-02-12, once everything has re-equilibrated; do not test immediately, you will measure the freezer and not the sample. Re-titre nothing, but assume the viable pellets are a last resort rather than a backup.

session_5.speaker: Lena Varga
session_5.text: [user, notes] Freezer alarm 2026-02-09, -80 corridor unit reached -62 C. Checked gDNA integrity three days after the alarm, on 2026-02-12: all six SCR-02 gDNA aliquots show high-molecular-weight DNA, DIN 8.9 to 9.2, no laddering. gDNA unaffected. The viable-frozen HAP1 pellets from the same shelf are now considered compromised and will not be used for validation work.

session_5.speaker: Dana Pryce
session_5.text: [attachment, email] From: Dana Pryce (Genomics Core). Subject: Brunello lot change. Lena - heads up, we have exhausted Brunello lot L-88213. The new lot is L-91007, received today 2026-02-11, and I have functionally titred it on HAP1 for you: 1.2e7 TU/mL. Anything you transduce from today onwards uses L-91007. The two lots are the same library design, different amplification batch, but the guide distribution differs slightly - L-91007 has a tighter Gini.

session_5.speaker: Lena Varga
session_5.text: Noting the library lot change: Brunello lot L-88213 is exhausted, lot L-91007 as of 2026-02-11, functional titre 1.2e7 TU/mL. SCR-01 and SCR-02 used L-88213. Everything from here uses L-91007. I will do a representation comparison two weeks after the lot change, so 2026-02-25, against the SCR-02 reference so that we know whether the lots are comparable before we pool anything across them.

session_5.speaker: assistant
session_5.text: [assistant, chat] Noted: lot L-91007 current from 2026-02-11, titre 1.2e7 TU/mL; representation comparison planned 2026-02-25, two weeks after the change. When you do that comparison, compare at the sgRNA level and not the gene level - a lot difference shows up as a shift in the guide count distribution long before it shows up in gene-level scores, and gene-level agreement will reassure you falsely.

session_5.speaker: Raul Mendes
session_5.text: [attachment, email] From: Raul Mendes. Subject: RUN-2601 QC. Gini index on the three day-7 references: 0.082, 0.079, 0.094. Zero-count guides: 0.4%, 0.5%, 0.7%. All within your thresholds. Mapping rate 71-78%, which is lowish but typical for this read structure. MAGeCK MLE paired is running now with replicate as covariate, FDR 0.1, as agreed. Preliminary: there is one very strong enriched gene and a long tail of nothing.

session_5.speaker: Lena Varga
session_5.text: One strong hit and nothing else is exactly the shape you want from a resistance screen with a bioactivated compound, and also exactly the shape an artifact takes. I will not quote the gene to Wei until the guide-level counts are looked at individually.

session_5.speaker: assistant
session_5.text: [assistant, chat] Right instinct. The specific artifact to exclude: a single resistant clone that expanded and whose PCR duplicates inflate the counts of whatever guide it happened to carry. Ask Mendes for the per-guide counts of the top gene in each replicate separately. If one guide carries the signal in one replicate and the others are flat, it is a clone, not a hit. If three of four guides move in all three replicates, it is real.

session_6.speaker: Lena Varga
session_6.text: Bad week. SCR-03, which was the replicate screen with the new lot L-91007, is contaminated. Mycoplasma positive by PCR on 2026-02-17, both the screen flasks and the HAP1 working stock. Everything in that incubator is going in the bin, I am thawing a fresh HAP1 vial from the master bank and SCR-03 is a failure. That is two failed screens now, SCR-01 for coverage and SCR-03 for contamination.

session_6.speaker: assistant
session_6.text: [assistant, chat] Two points, one procedural and one about interpretation. Procedural: thaw the fresh vial into a different incubator and test it at day 3 and day 10 before it touches a screen - mycoplasma from a shared incubator reappears about a third of the time, and you do not want to discover that after another transduction. On interpretation: SCR-02 was harvested on 2026-02-08, before the first positive test, so its data are not automatically suspect, but you should test a retained SCR-02 pellet before you build a paper on that hit.

session_6.speaker: Lena Varga
session_6.text: [user, notes] SCR-03 post mortem. Mycoplasma positive 2026-02-17 by PCR, confirmed on repeat. Affected: SCR-03 flasks (day 4 of selection), HAP1 working stock P14. Discarded 2026-02-18. Library lot L-91007 vector prep itself tested negative, so the lot is not the source. Retained SCR-02 pellet tested negative, so SCR-02 data stand. Fresh HAP1 thawed from master bank into the second incubator, now P2. No sequencing run consumed by SCR-03.

session_6.speaker: Wei Chen
session_6.text: [attachment, email] From: Wei Chen. Subject: re: mycoplasma. Lena - annoying but handled correctly. Two asks. (1) Everyone in the lab tests their lines monthly from now on, please write the one-paragraph policy. (2) For the grant report due in May I need the number of screens attempted and the number that produced usable data, so keep that tally explicit rather than reconstructing it later. Also: Ilse Brandt wants to be a co-author on the screen paper, which I think is reasonable given the compound. Let us discuss.

session_6.speaker: Lena Varga
session_6.text: Separate protocol change while I am rewriting the SOP anyway. The 56 C for 1 h proteinase K lysis in Section 6.2 gives me variable yields on big pellets - 4e7 cells does not fully lyse in an hour. Switching to 55 C overnight, which is what the Genomics Core does for their own extractions.

session_6.speaker: assistant
session_6.text: [assistant, chat] Sensible, and the lower temperature with the longer time is the better trade for high-molecular-weight yield. Updated protocol step, in your format. 6.2 Resuspend the pellet in proteinase K buffer and incubate at **55 C overnight** (14-18 h) with gentle agitation, replacing the former 56 C for 1 h. 6.3 Do not vortex after lysis; invert. One consequence to plan around: your gDNA now arrives a day later than it used to, so a harvest on a Thursday means extraction read on a Friday, and you have told me nothing starts on a Friday.

session_6.speaker: SOP-HAP1-CRISPR-v3.md

session_8.speaker: assistant

session_10.speaker: assistant
session_10.text: [assistant, chat] Two recommendations. For the screen: sequence to **300x** library coverage rather than 500x. At 77,441 guides that is about 23 million reads per library, and the gain from 300x to 500x is small compared with the gain from having spent those reads on an extra replicate - the limiting noise in your screen is biological, not sampling. Keep 500x as the cell-number target at every culture step; it is only the sequencing depth I would drop. For the RNA-seq: 45 million read pairs per sample. That is enough for differential expression of moderately expressed genes with three replicates, and going to 80 million buys you only low-abundance transcripts you are not asking about.

session_12.speaker: assistant

Recommendation: do not re-sequence the existing libraries, re-prepare them with unique dual indexes from the retained gDNA. Hopping happens at the loading and clustering stage, so re-sequencing the same single-indexed libraries on the same chemistry reproduces the problem exactly. domain: pure mathematics (low-dimensional topology / geometric group theory)

session_1.speaker: Mara Ellison
session_1.text: Starting a new project file with you. I'm a postdoc at Bonn working on a paper with two co-authors: Tomas Ibarra (Universidad de Santiago) and Priya Raman (University of Bristol). Working title: 'Acylindrical actions on arc-like complexes for free-by-cyclic groups'. The object of study is a complex I'm currently calling X(Gamma) built from the Bass-Serre tree of the ascending HNN extension. Theorem A gives an acylindricity constant kappa = 14 for the action of F_n rtimes_phi Z on X(Gamma) when phi is irreducible with no periodic conjugacy classes. We are aiming at Geometry & Topology, special issue.

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text: [assistant, chat] Noted. Project frame: paper on acylindrical actions for free-by-cyclic groups, complex X(Gamma), Theorem A with kappa = 14, co-authors Tomas Ibarra (Santiago) and Priya Raman (Bristol), target Geometry & Topology special issue. I will track notation, constants, hypotheses and deadlines as they change. Two things I'd want pinned early: (1) whether acylindricity is uniform over the automorphism or only over the fixed phi, and (2) whether X(Gamma) is connected for n = 2, where the arc graph degenerates.

session_1.speaker: Mara Ellison
session_1.text: [user, notes] Notation table v1. Gamma = finite graph with one vertex and n edges. X(Gamma) = arc-like complex, vertices = isotopy classes of essential arcs, edges = disjointness. T(Gamma) = Bass-Serre tree. kappa = 14 = acylindricity constant in Theorem A. K = 14 is separately the injectivity-radius bound in Section 2 (same number, unrelated quantity - do not conflate). delta = 6 hyperbolicity constant for X(Gamma) from Lemma 2.7.

session_1.speaker: draft-v0.3.tex
session_1.text: [attachment, document] Excerpt, draft-v0.3.tex, Section 1. THEOREM A. Let phi in Out(F_n) be irreducible with no periodic conjugacy classes, n >= 3, and let G = F_n rtimes_phi Z. Then G acts acylindrically on X(Gamma): for every epsilon > 0 there is R = R(epsilon) such that for all x, y in X(Gamma) with d(x,y) >= R, the set of g in G with d(x,gx) <= epsilon and d(y,gy) <= epsilon has cardinality at most kappa = 14. Remark 1.2: we do not know whether kappa can be taken independent of n.

session_1.speaker: Mara Ellison
session_1.text: A standing request about how you give me things. When you give me a proof sketch, I want it as numbered steps, one claim per step, and I want the hypotheses restated explicitly at the top of the sketch even if we just discussed them. No flowing prose paragraphs - I lose track of where a hypothesis got used, and that is exactly where my errors live.

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text: [assistant, chat] Understood - numbered steps, hypotheses restated at the top, no prose. Sketch for Lemma 3.4 in that format. Hypotheses: H1, H subgroup of F_n; H2, phi irreducible with no periodic conjugacy classes; H3, H of finite index in F_n (as currently written in your draft). Step 1. H acts on T(Gamma) with quotient a finite graph of groups. Step 2. Pick two hyperbolic elements a, b in H with disjoint axis-endpoint pairs in partial T(Gamma). Step 3. Run a ping-pong argument on T(Gamma) with the four disjoint endpoint neighbourhoods. Step 4. Conclude a, b generate a free subgroup of rank 2 whose orbit map to X(Gamma) is a quasi-isometric embedding. Step 5. Transport the bound back to X(Gamma) using Lemma 2.7. I would run this through the Bass-Serre tree rather than directly in X(Gamma): the tree gives you honest disjointness and the complex only gives you coarse disjointness.

(2) Can we state Theorem B for all ascending HNN extensions or only the geometric ones? session_2.speaker: Mara Ellison
session_2.text: Counterexample. Conjecture B as stated in draft-v0.3 is false. I built a mapping torus of a pseudo-Anosov on a closed surface - I believe genus 2 - whose fundamental group is free-by-cyclic but where the orbit map to X(Gamma) has quasi-isometric constants blowing up along a sequence of powers. The dilatation is lambda = 1.83929 (largest root of x^3 - x^2 - x - 1). So the 'uniform in phi' clause in Conjecture B has to go.

session_2.speaker: assistant
session_2.text: [assistant, chat] That is the right shape for a counterexample to a uniformity claim. Two checks before you commit it to the draft. (1) Confirm the surface genus from the Euler characteristic of your train track, not from the picture - a genus-2 closed surface gives chi = -2 and rank 4 free group on the once-punctured version, and your stated edge count looked like chi = -4. session_4.speaker: assistant
session_4.text: [assistant, chat] Under 35 U.S.C. 315(e)(2), once the Board issues a final written decision on a claim, Kestrel is estopped in the district court from asserting that the claim is invalid on any ground it raised or reasonably could have raised in the IPR, i.e. patents and printed publications. Practically: Tanaka, Brandt and Novak-based obviousness would be estopped for any claim reaching a final written decision; the Halberg thesis likely too if it's a printed publication. System-art (e.g., a physical prior LiDAR product) is not estopped, though California Institute of Technology v. Broadcom, 25 F.4th 976 (Fed. Cir. 2022), broadened 'reasonably could have raised'. Estoppel only attaches on final written decisions, and only for instituted claims.

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text: [assistant, chat] Crisp justification: a 500-day (roughly two-year) lookback balances responsiveness and stability. At 99% confidence, 250 days gives only 2.5 tail observations, so the VaR estimate jumps when single days enter or leave the window; 500 days puts VaR at the 5th worst loss, which halves that sensitivity while still reflecting the current volatility regime more than a 3-5 year window would. session_4.speaker: Mara Lindqvist
session_4.text: Quick sanity check: Rachel asked over the phone whether a 1.0 beta proxy overstates or understates risk for Harbor Point. My view is it understates because the loan's spread vol is higher than the index. Right?

session_4.speaker: assistant
session_4.text: [assistant, chat] Mostly right, with nuance. A beta of 1.0 to CDX HY captures only the systematic component; if the loan's true beta is above 1.0 the systematic risk is understated, and in all cases the idiosyncratic component (residual variance) is missing entirely. Total spread variance = beta^2 * sigma_index^2 + sigma_resid^2. For a single-name leveraged loan, residual variance is often 40-60% of the total. So the 1.0 proxy understates risk unless the loan's true beta is well below 1.0 and its residual vol is small, which is unlikely for a stressed issuer like Harbor Point. One offsetting point: loans trade with lagged, smoothed marks, so the observed historical vol may itself be understated.

session_8.text: For PBC-25 I need the breach log out of Snowflake. Table risk.limit_utilisation has as_of_date, limit_id, desk, metric, value, limit_value, limit_type ('hard'/'soft'). I want each hard breach episode once, i.e. the first day a hard limit goes over 100%, not every consecutive day. Write the SQL.

session_8.speaker: assistant
session_8.text:
[assistant, chat] ```sql
WITH u AS (
  SELECT as_of_date, limit_id, desk, metric, value, limit_value,
         value / NULLIF(limit_value, 0) AS util,
         LAG(value / NULLIF(limit_value, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY limit_id ORDER BY as_of_date) AS prev_util
  FROM risk.limit_utilisation
  WHERE limit_type = 'hard'
    AND as_of_date BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2026-02-28'
)
SELECT as_of_date AS breach_start, limit_id, desk, metric,
       ROUND(value, 1) AS value, limit_value, ROUND(100 * util, 1) AS util_pct
FROM u
WHERE util > 1.0
  AND (prev_util IS NULL OR prev_util <= 1.0)
ORDER BY as_of_date;
```
The LAG(...) OVER (PARTITION BY limit_id ORDER BY as_of_date) picks up the prior day's utilisation for the same limit, so only the first day of each episode is returned. Caveat: LAG uses the prior row, not the prior business day; if a limit has missing days, use a gaps-and-islands approach with a business-day calendar.

session_10.speaker: Mara Lindqvist
session_10.text: Different topic. Rachel asked, informally, whether we have considered moving from VaR 99% to expected shortfall 97.5% like FRTB. What's the relationship under normality? I want to say something sensible.

session_10.speaker: assistant
session_10.text: [assistant, chat] Under normality with zero mean: VaR_99 = z_0.99 * sigma = 2.326 sigma. ES_97.5 = sigma * phi(z_0.975) / 0.025 = sigma * phi(1.960)/0.025 = sigma * 0.05845/0.025 = 2.338 sigma. So ES_97.5 / VaR_99 is about 1.005: under normality the two measures are almost identical, which is why the Basel Committee chose 97.5% ES as the replacement calibration. The difference shows up with fat tails: for a Student-t with 4 degrees of freedom (scaled to unit variance) ES_97.5 is about 1.06 to 1.08 times VaR_99. For your historical simulation, ES_97.5 at 500 days is the average of the worst 12.5 scenario losses (interpolating the 13th), versus VaR_99 at the 5th worst; that average uses more tail information and is less sensitive to a single scenario, but has higher estimation error with only 12-13 points.

session_10.speaker: Mara Lindqvist
session_10.text: Give me a function to compute historical VaR and ES from the scenario P&L vector, same style as before.

session_10.speaker: assistant
session_10.text:
[assistant, chat] ```python
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


def hist_var_es(pnl: pd.Series, var_conf: float = 0.99, es_conf: float = 0.975) -> dict[str, float]:
    losses = np.sort(-pnl.to_numpy())[::-1]  # largest loss first
    n = losses.size
    k_var = int(np.ceil(n * (1 - var_conf)))
    var = float(losses[k_var - 1])
    tail = n * (1 - es_conf)
    k = int(np.floor(tail))
    es = float((losses[:k].sum() + (tail - k) * losses[k]) / tail)
    return {"var": var, "es": es, "n": float(n)}


def main() -> None:
    pnl = pd.read_parquet("scenario_pnl_2025-12-31.parquet")["pnl"]
    print(hist_var_es(pnl))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
With 500 scenarios, k_var = 5 (5th worst loss) and the ES tail is 12.5 scenarios, so the 13th worst loss gets half weight.

from __future__ import annotations
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm


def estimate_beta(spread_chg: pd.Series, proxy_chg: pd.Series, window: int = 36, floor: float = 0.8) -> tuple[float, float]:
    df = pd.concat([spread_chg, proxy_chg], axis=1, keys=["y", "x"]).dropna().tail(window)
    res = sm.OLS(df["y"], sm.add_constant(df["x"])).fit()
    beta = max(float(res.params["x"]), floor)
    resid_vol = float(res.resid.std(ddof=1))
    return beta, resid_vol


def main() -> None:
    spreads = pd.read_parquet("monthly_spread_changes.parquet")
    for name in ["HARBOR_POINT_TLB"]:
        print(name, estimate_beta(spreads[name], spreads["BUCKET_B_CHEM"]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

SELECT as_of_date, factor_id, ret,
       CASE WHEN as_of_date BETWEEN '2008-09-01' AND '2009-08-31' THEN 'GFC_2008'

session_1.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_1.text: Kicking off structural calcs for HOS-2417, Alder Street Commons in Tacoma. Eight stories: Level 1 retail podium with a steel transfer level at L2 on concrete spread footings, Levels 3-8 glulam post-and-beam with CLT floor panels, Type IV-B construction, roof at L8. Lateral system is steel buckling-restrained braced frames (BRBF) in the two stair/elevator cores. Design basis I'm carrying for the superstructure: 2021 IBC with Washington amendments, ASCE 7-16, NDS 2018, AISC 360-16 and AISC 341-16. Ridgeline Geotechnical's preliminary report says Site Class C. Ground snow 25 psf, Risk Category II. Seismic weight from the Revit takeoff is W = 8,640 kips, h_n = 92 ft. For ASCE 7-16 Site Class C the hazard tool gives SDS = 0.91 g and SD1 = 0.50 g. Can you set up the equivalent lateral force base shear for the BRBF (R = 8, Omega_o = 2.5, Cd = 5)?

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text: [assistant, chat] Equivalent lateral force, ASCE 7-16 Section 12.8. Approximate period: Ta = Ct * h_n^x = 0.03 * 92^0.75 = 0.89 s (BRBF uses Ct = 0.03, x = 0.75 per Table 12.8-2). Cs = SDS/(R/Ie) = 0.91/(8/1.0) = 0.114, but it need not exceed SD1/(T*(R/Ie)) = 0.50/(0.89 * 8) = 0.0702. Minimum Cs = 0.044*SDS*Ie = 0.040 (and S1 < 0.6 g so Eq. 12.8-6 does not apply). Governing Cs = 0.0702. Base shear V = Cs*W = 0.0702 * 8,640 kips = 607 kips. Vertical distribution exponent k = 1.0 + (0.89 - 0.5)/2 = 1.20. Design story drift limit for Risk Category II, structure over 4 stories: Delta_a = 0.020 h_sx. Note: if you later get a computed period from the ETABS model you may use Cu*Ta = 1.4*0.89 = 1.25 s as the cap for strength, which would reduce Cs further, but I'd keep 0.89 s until the model is calibrated.

session_1.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_1.text: Good. Gravity framing assumptions for the typical residential floors L3-L8: CLT floor panels 5-ply 175 mm grade V2 spanning about 19 ft between glulam beams, 3 in normalweight concrete topping over an acoustic mat, superimposed dead 15 psf, partitions 15 psf, residential live 40 psf, corridors 100 psf. Glulam is 24F-V8 DF/DF for beams and girders, 24F-1.8E? no, columns are Combination 2 DF. Can you sanity-check the floor self-weight?

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text: [assistant, chat] Self-weight check: 5-ply 175 mm (6.89 in) V2 CLT at roughly 31 pcf = 6.89/12 * 31 = 17.8 psf. 3 in normalweight topping at 150 pcf = 37.5 psf. Acoustic mat about 1 psf. Glulam beams/girders smeared at about 5 psf. Total structural dead load is about 61 psf, plus 15 psf superimposed and 15 psf partitions = 91 psf for gravity design (partition load is live per ASCE 7 Section 4.3.2 but include at least 10 psf in seismic weight per 12.7.2). That is consistent with your 8,640 kips seismic weight if the floor plate is around 16,500 sf. One caution: 175 mm V2 at a 19 ft span will be governed by vibration rather than bending; I'd flag that before the peer reviewer does.

session_1.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_1.text: One more: what's the redundancy factor situation for the BRBF cores? Two frames per direction per core, so four per direction total.

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text: [assistant, chat] With two cores and two BRB frames per direction in each core (four per direction), removal of any one brace typically won't cause more than a 33% reduction in story strength and won't create an extreme torsional irregularity, so you can usually justify rho = 1.0 under ASCE 7-16 Section 12.3.4.2 condition (a), provided the cores are reasonably balanced in plan. If the north core frames carry noticeably more than half the story shear in the ETABS run, check the brace-removal case explicitly; otherwise use rho = 1.3 conservatively for the collectors and frames. Collectors and their connections still need the overstrength factor Omega_o = 2.5 per Section 12.10.2.1 for SDC D.

session_1.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_1.text: Wind for the MWFRS: basic wind speed V = 98 mph (Risk Category II), Exposure B, Kzt = 1.0. Does wind come anywhere close to governing over seismic for the BRBs?

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text: [assistant, chat] Rough check: for a 92 ft (28.0 m) building, Exposure B, V = 98 mph (44 m/s), the velocity pressure at roof height is qh = 0.00256*Kz*Kzt*Ke*V^2 = 0.00256*0.98*1.0*1.0*98^2 = 24.1 psf (1.15 kPa). With a net pressure coefficient of about 1.3 on a 150 ft (45.7 m) wide face, the strength-level wind base shear is roughly 300-330 kips (1,330-1,470 kN) per direction, about half of the 607 kips (2,700 kN) seismic. Seismic governs the BRBs; wind will matter for cladding, drift serviceability and roof uplift on the CLT roof panels.

With Lb = 10 ft (3.05 m), slightly over Lp, both sections are close to the plastic moment. W30x116 (Zx = 378 in^3): phi*Mn about 1,390 kip-ft (1,885 kN-m) after the small LTB reduction, DCR = 1.11, does not work. session_3.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_3.text: Fire design question. Type IV-B needs a 2-hour rating on the primary frame (columns, girders) and on floor construction. Exposed glulam will be designed by the NDS Chapter 16 calculated method. Nominal char rate beta_n = 1.5 in/hr. What effective char depth do I take for 2 hours, and what's the formula?

session_3.speaker: assistant
session_3.text: [assistant, chat] NDS 2018 Section 16.2.1: beta_t = beta_n / t^0.187 where t is in hours but the nominal rate is defined at 1 hr, so beta_t = 1.5 in/hr. Char depth a_char = beta_t * t^0.813 = 1.5 * 2^0.813 = 2.64 in (67 mm). Effective char depth a_eff = 1.2 * a_char = 3.2 in (81 mm) for a 2-hour exposure, which matches NDS Table 16.2.1A. For reference, the same table gives 1.8 in (46 mm) for 1 hour and 2.5 in (64 mm) for 1.5 hours. Apply a_eff to every exposed face, then check the residual section with the NDS Table 16.2.2 design stress to member strength factors (2.85 for bending and tension, 2.58 for compression parallel to grain, 2.03 for beam and column buckling). Don't forget the outer lam rule: for glulam bending members designed for fire, replace one core lam with one tension lam per NDS 16.2.4.

session_3.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_3.text: So for the C/3-4 girder exposed on three sides, 8-3/4 x 24, what's the residual section?

session_3.speaker: assistant
session_3.text: [assistant, chat] Three-sided exposure (top protected by the CLT and topping): residual width b_r = 8.75 - 2*3.2 = 2.35 in (60 mm), residual depth d_r = 24 - 3.2 = 20.8 in (528 mm). S_r = 2.35*20.8^2/6 = 169 in^3 (2,770 cm^3). Fire load combination is D + L (no load factors for the ASD fire check) with M = 117 kip-ft (159 kN-m): fb = 117*12/169 = 8.31 ksi (57.3 MPa). Allowable for fire = 2.85 * Fb * CV * ... = 2.85*2.40*0.95 = 6.50 ksi (44.8 MPa). DCR = 1.28 for 2-hr. The 8-3/4 width is too narrow for a 2-hour three-sided exposure; you'll need 10-3/4 or encapsulation (two layers of 5/8 Type X on the girder sides would get you there per 2021 IBC 722.7 but Marcus wants it exposed).

session_3.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_3.text: Marcus says the exposed ceiling area in the amenity lounge will be about 18% of the L3 ceiling. Is that OK for Type IV-B?

session_3.speaker: assistant
session_3.text: [assistant, chat] Under the 2021 IBC Section 602.4.2.2.2 (Type IV-B), unprotected mass timber ceilings (including attached beams) are limited to 20% of the floor area in any dwelling unit or fire area, and exposed beams and columns are permitted within that limit provided they meet the required fire-resistance rating by calculation. 18% is within the limit. The C/3-4 girder exposure counts toward the 20%, and the girder still needs the 2-hour rating by calculation, which is why the 8-3/4 width is a problem.

session_4.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_4.text: Great. So we're redesigning to ASCE 7-22. What actually changes for us besides the seismic numbers? I need to explain this to Carla for the additional services request.

session_4.speaker: assistant
session_4.text: [assistant, chat] Main ASCE 7-22 impacts for this building: (1) Seismic: new multi-period response spectra and new site classes (BC, CD, DE added); SDS/SD1 come from the USGS hazard tool directly and generally go up for Puget Sound soft-rock sites. (2) Snow: ground snow loads are now reliability-targeted, strength-level values from the ASCE hazard tool, and the LRFD snow load factor drops to 1.0, so pg numbers look bigger than 7-16 values but factored loads change less than they appear. (3) Wind: minor changes; ground elevation factor Ke and tornado loads don't apply to Risk Category II. (4) Collector and diaphragm design: Section 12.10.3 alternative diaphragm design provisions may be attractive for the CLT diaphragm. (5) Drift and stability: no major change for BRBF. Expect the BRBs, collectors and the steel transfer level to see the biggest changes.

session_4.speaker: Ridgeline Geotechnical
session_4.text: [attachment, document] Geotechnical Report Revision 1, Alder Street Commons, Project RG-26-118, dated 2026-06-05 (excerpt). Section 6.2 (revised): A multichannel analysis of surface waves (MASW) survey was performed on 2026-05-27 along two lines. Measured Vs30 = 1,080 ft/s. Under ASCE 7-22 Table 20.2-1 this corresponds to Site Class CD (1,000 to 1,450 ft/s). This supersedes the Site Class C estimate in our preliminary report dated 2026-03-20. Foundation recommendations in Section 7 are unchanged (6,000 psf allowable bearing).

session_4.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_4.text: Ran the ASCE hazard tool for Site Class CD and Risk Category II at the site: SDS = 1.02 g, SD1 = 0.62 g, ground snow pg = 32 psf (up from the 25 psf we used under 7-16). Same W = 8,640 kips. Please redo the base shear and the flat roof snow.

session_4.speaker: assistant
session_4.text: [assistant, chat] ASCE 7-22 ELF with SDS = 1.02 g, SD1 = 0.62 g: Ta = 0.89 s (unchanged). Cs = SDS/(R/Ie) = 1.02/8 = 0.128, capped at SD1/(T*R/Ie) = 0.62/(0.89*8) = 0.0871. Cs,min = 0.044*1.02 = 0.045. Governing Cs = 0.0871. V = 0.0871 * 8,640 = 752 kips (3,345 kN), up from 607 kips (2,700 kN) under ASCE 7-16, an increase of about 24%. Flat roof snow: pf = 0.7*Ce*Ct*Is*pg = 0.7*1.0*1.0*1.0*32 = 22.4 psf (1.07 kPa), versus 17.5 psf (0.84 kPa) previously; with the LRFD snow factor at 1.0 under 7-22 the factored roof snow is 22.4 psf vs 1.6*17.5 = 28.0 psf under 7-16, so the roof actually gets slightly lighter in LRFD. Rain-on-snow surcharge does not apply (pg > 20 psf).

session_4.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_4.text: BRB-3 at Level 2 north core currently has a 6.5 in^2 yielding core, DCR 0.83 under the 7-16 forces. What do we need now?

session_4.speaker: assistant
session_4.text: [assistant, chat] Scaling the brace force by 752/607 = 1.24: DCR = 0.83*1.24 = 1.03 with the 6.5 in^2 (4,190 mm^2) core. To get back to about 0.95, Asc required = 6.5*1.03/0.95 = 7.05 in^2. I'd recommend going to 7.25 in^2 (4,680 mm^2), which is a standard Restrain Dynamics core plate size, giving DCR = 0.92 and leaving room for the accidental torsion update. Remember that the adjusted brace strength (beta*omega*Ry*Fysc*Asc) drives the gusset, beam and column capacity design, so a bigger core increases the demands on the L2 transfer girders too; re-run the capacity design rather than just swapping the core.

session_5.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_5.text: For the two short anchor rods at 2/B, is a coupler nut really OK for F1554 Grade 105 under BRB uplift?

session_5.speaker: assistant
session_5.text: [assistant, chat] Yes, if the coupler is a heavy hex coupling nut with a proof load at least equal to the rod's specified minimum tensile strength (F1554 Gr 105: Fu = 125 ksi, so for 1-1/4 in (32 mm) rods, Ab*Fu = 1.227*125 = 153 kips (681 kN)) and the extension rod is the same grade. Detail 12/S-501 shows this. session_6.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_6.text: Castellan's peer review letter came in yesterday. 23 comments. The two that matter: PR-09 on floor vibration of the 175 mm CLT at the 19 ft spans, and PR-14 on long-term deflection of the L3 grid C girder with the mezzanine equipment treated as sustained load. Everything else is drafting and connection detailing. Let's start with PR-09.

session_6.speaker: Castellan Engineering
session_6.text: [attachment, document] Castellan Engineering, Structural Peer Review Letter No. 1, Alder Street Commons (BLD26-0412), dated 2026-06-23, reviewer Priya Raman, SE (excerpt). PR-09: The 5-ply 175 mm V2 CLT floor panels at 19 ft clear span appear to have a fundamental frequency below commonly accepted thresholds for residential occupancy. Provide a vibration evaluation per the U.S. CLT Handbook Chapter 7 or AISC Design Guide 11 adapted method. PR-14: The grid C/3-4 girder at Level 3 supports mechanical equipment that is permanently installed; treat equipment weight as sustained load in the long-term deflection check with Kcr = 1.5 and confirm compliance with L/240. PR-17: Provide BRB gusset plate buckling check per Thornton method with K = 0.6 for the compact gussets. PR-21: Clarify spline screw spacing at CLT diaphragm panel joints. Total comments: 23.

session_6.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_6.text: For PR-09: 5-ply 175 mm V2, span 19 ft simply supported, topping 3 in NW, my target is f1 of at least 8.0 Hz. What does it come out to?

session_6.speaker: assistant
session_6.text: [assistant, chat] Using f1 = (pi/(2*L^2)) * sqrt(EI_eff/m), with EI_eff for 175 mm V2 about 440e6 lbf-in^2/ft (Cascadia's published value) and mass including the 3 in topping and 15 psf SDL: f1 = 7.6 Hz for the 175 mm V2 panels, below your 8.0 Hz target. Options: (a) 5-ply 191 mm E1, EI_eff about 640e6 lbf-in^2/ft, gives f1 = 9.1 Hz; (b) 7-ply 245 mm V2 gives about 11.3 Hz but adds 4.3 psf and 2 in of depth; (c) add a mid-span glulam beam, which Marcus will hate. I recommend option (a): 5-ply 191 mm E1 at 9.1 Hz meets the target with 0.63 in (16 mm) more depth than the 175 mm. Also confirm with the CLT Handbook span criterion L_lim = 0.11*(EI_eff)^0.29/m^0.12 as a cross-check; for the E1 191 mm it gives about 20.4 ft, above the 19 ft span.

session_6.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_6.text: Go with 5-ply 191 mm E1 for all typical floor panels L3-L8. Roof stays 5-ply 175 mm V2 since there's no topping and no occupancy vibration concern. I'll update the spec section 06 17 19 and tell Cascadia. Now PR-21: what screw recommendation should I put on the diaphragm detail?

session_6.speaker: assistant
session_6.text: [assistant, chat] For the CLT diaphragm surface splines (1 in x 5-1/2 in plywood or LVL spline over the panel joint), I recommend 8 mm x 160 mm partially threaded self-tapping screws at 6 in (150 mm) on center in two rows (one row each side of the joint), each row staggered 3 in (75 mm). That gives a nominal shear capacity in the range of 1,100 plf (16.1 kN/m) per joint at ASD after applying the 0.85 ductility reduction used in the Section 12.10.3 alternative diaphragm design, which covers the 7-22 diaphragm forces for the typical floors. At the collectors near the cores the demand is higher; tighten to 4 in (100 mm) on center within 8 ft of the core walls. Specify screws with an ICC-ES evaluation report and require 5% field verification of embedment by Northgate.

session_7.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_7.text: PR-14 now. Treat the mezzanine equipment as sustained. Equipment is 8.8 kips of the 14.2 kips per point, plus the original 4.6 kips structure dead. Redo long-term deflection for the 8-3/4 x 24 and tell me what size gets us under L/240.

session_7.speaker: assistant
session_7.text: [assistant, chat] Sustained load per point = 4.6 + 8.8 = 13.4 kips (59.6 kN); transient = 0.8 kips. For 8-3/4 x 24 (I = 10,080 in^4, E = 1,800 ksi): Delta_sustained = 0.62 in, Delta_LT = Kcr*Delta_sustained + Delta_transient = 1.5*0.62 + 0.04 + self-weight creep 0.30 = 1.27 in (32 mm) > L/240 = 1.20 in (30 mm). Fails. Also, from the May fire check, the 8-3/4 width already fails the 2-hour three-sided exposure at DCR 1.28. A 10-3/4 x 27 24F-V8 (I = 17,630 in^4) gives Delta_LT = 0.73 in (19 mm) = L/395 and 2-hour residual section 4.35 in x 23.8 in, DCR 0.71 in fire. A 10-3/4 x 25-1/2 would pass deflection at 0.86 in but only gets fire DCR 0.93. I recommend 10-3/4 x 27, which also respects Marcus's 27 in maximum depth.

session_11.text: Northgate is going to verify the BRB gusset bolt pretension at the L2 north core next Tuesday. Those gusset connections at BRB-3 use 7/8 in A325 (ASTM F3125 Grade A325) in standard holes, slip-critical Class A. session_11.speaker: assistant
session_11.text: [assistant, chat] Per AISC 360-16 Table J3.1 (minimum bolt pretension, Group A bolts): 7/8 in A325 = 39 kips (173 kN); 3/4 in A325 = 28 kips (125 kN). For the RCSC 2020 pre-installation verification, the calibrated wrench or turn-of-nut must achieve at least 1.05 times those values in the Skidmore-Wilhelm, i.e. 41 kips (182 kN) for the 7/8 in and 29 kips (131 kN) for the 3/4 in. If they're using turn-of-nut, rotation from snug-tight is 1/3 turn for bolt lengths up to 4d (3-1/2 in for 7/8 in bolts) and 1/2 turn for lengths over 4d up to 8d. The kicker bolts per RFI-015 are bearing-type (A325-N) and only need snug-tight, so Northgate doesn't need to verify pretension on those.

session_11.speaker: Sam Whitaker
session_11.text: [attachment, email] Subject: Revised drift table (ASCE 7-22, Site Class CD, W = 8,190 k). Allowable 2.0% for Risk Category II. Torsional irregularity ratio 1.16 at L4, below 1.2 so no Type 1a. Redundancy rho = 1.0 justified per 12.3.4.2(a); brace removal case gives 22% strength loss. Sam

session_11.speaker: assistant
session_11.text: [assistant, chat] Checks out: 1.42% at L4 is 71% of the 2.0% Risk Category II limit (Table 12.12-1 for structures over 4 stories other than masonry). One note on Sam's email: the drift in inches at L4 should be 0.0142*10.5 ft*12 = 1.79 in (45 mm), not 1.69 in; the percentage is right, the inch value looks like it was computed with the old 10.0 ft story height. Torsional ratio 1.16 < 1.2 means no Type 1a irregularity and accidental torsion amplification Ax = (1.16/1.2)^2 = 0.93, use 1.0. Deformation compatibility for the glulam gravity columns at 1.42% drift: confirm the column-to-beam connections can tolerate about 0.014 rad rotation; the knife-plate connections in 9/S-503 typically can.

session_12.text: S-052 CLT panel layout shows 2-1/2 in bearing at grid D for the 191 mm panels. The drawings say 3 in minimum. Is 2-1/2 actually OK structurally, if I wanted to be flexible?

session_12.speaker: assistant
session_12.text: [assistant, chat] Bearing check at grid D: panel reaction about 1.9 kips/ft (27.7 kN/m) D+L. Bearing perpendicular to grain on the glulam (Fc_perp = 650 psi (4.5 MPa)): required length = 1,900/(12*650) = 0.24 in (6 mm), so 2-1/2 in (64 mm) is fine for stress. The 3 in minimum is about erection tolerance (+/- 1/2 in panel length tolerance and glulam sweep), edge distance for the panel-to-beam screws (at least 1-1/2 in from the panel end), and the fire-rated joint between panel end and beam. With 2-1/2 in nominal and a 1/2 in short tolerance you would be at 2 in, which compromises the screw edge distance. I'd hold 3 in; Revise and Resubmit is appropriate.

session_14.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_14.text: Then the RTU thing. Four RTUs at 4,850 lb each on a steel dunnage frame, bearing on the L8 roof glulam beams at four points per unit. The roof is 5-ply 175 mm V2 with no topping. Quick check whether the roof beams under it (6-3/4 x 19-1/2 24F-V8 at 22 ft span) can take it.

session_14.speaker: assistant
session_14.text: [assistant, chat] Per RTU: 4,850 lb (21.6 kN) over four dunnage points = 1,213 lb (5.4 kN) per point; assume two points land on each beam at roughly the third points. Added moment per beam = 1.21*22/3 = 8.9 kip-ft (12.1 kN-m). Existing roof beam D + S moment (with S = 22.4 psf at 10 ft tributary): about 31 kip-ft (42 kN-m). Total 39.9 kip-ft. 6-3/4 x 19-1/2: S = 428 in^3, fb = 39.9*12/428 = 1.12 ksi (7.7 MPa) vs F'b = 2.40*1.0 (CD for snow 1.15 -> 2.76 ksi) * CV 0.96 = 2.65 ksi. DCR = 0.42. OK. Check the dunnage support detail for local bearing on the beam top (perpendicular-to-grain, Fc_perp = 650 psi): a 4 in x 6 in bearing plate gives 1,213/24 = 51 psi, fine. Also confirm the mechanical engineer's operating weight; 4,850 lb sounds like shipping weight and operating may be higher.

session_15.speaker: assistant
session_15.text: [assistant, chat] Assessment: a 2-1/4 in (57 mm) deep split in a 10-3/4 in wide column below a beam seat mainly reduces shear and bearing capacity locally and can propagate under seasonal drying. Axial capacity of 10-3/4 x 10-1/2 Comb. 2 DF at L4 with 118 kips (525 kN) demand: P'c is about 195 kips, DCR 0.61, and a single split of this depth doesn't change the axial capacity significantly. But the seat connection relies on the screws within 18 in of the beam seat. Suggested disposition: reinforce with two rows of four 8 mm x 300 mm fully threaded self-tapping screws installed perpendicular to the split, at 3 in (76 mm) spacing, starting 4 in above the split end, and fill the check with a structural epoxy only if Studio Fenwick wants it cosmetically. Northgate to measure the split width again in 60 days; if it grows beyond 1/2 in, replace the column segment. I'd keep the column in place.

session_16.speaker: Dana Okafor
session_16.text: Also, Sam asked why we didn't need to reduce the BRB cores after the topping change dropped the base shear. Remind me what you told me then.

session_16.speaker: assistant
session_16.text: [assistant, chat] When the topping change dropped V from 752 kips (3,345 kN) to 713 kips (3,172 kN), I advised not to downsize the BRB cores: BRB-3 was at 7.25 in^2 (4,680 mm^2), its DCR only fell to about 0.87, and the capacity design of the L2 transfer girders, gussets and columns had already been completed with the 7.25 in^2 adjusted brace strength. Downsizing would have required redoing the capacity design and re-issuing the BRB shop drawings (S-044A was already approved) for little benefit. The extra margin also covers the accidental torsion and any future ETABS model refinement.
